correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and nonempty fixed sensor set, the direct walk expansion yields the exact single-site Krylov span generated by reflection-symmetric two-point rows, with even-ring antipodal cancellation. Intersection of their annihilators is characterized by finite dihedral reflection orbits; gcd(n,2(s-s0)) reduces it to quotient sizes g or 2g and nullities floor(g/2) or g-1. The lower-bound rank count and complete first-Krylov-vector span give the sharp ceil(n/2) time horizon for coprime pairs. Mobius inversion on the gcd condition yields all binomial counts. Independently implemented direct Rule-90 evolution and GF2 rank checks matched the formula across all 4079 subsets of sizes3..11 and 1520 random larger tests; these are corroboration only.
